new_packages.description: A cluster centered on הטבע (the natural order, natural determinism) as the opposing force to prayer and divine providence. This package groups: (1) הטבע itself — the fixed, compelled order of nature; (2) אם כל חי — the philosophical name for nature as the ultimate source of life; (3) מינים/אפיקורסים — the heretics and Epicureans who embody the naturalistic worldview. The common denominator is the claim that nature is supreme and that divine intervention/miracle does not exist. This is the structural evil mirror of the prayer/transcendence package.
new_packages.why_potentially_new: Across the analyzed Torahs (1-35, 100+), the standard evil mirror packages are: יצר הרע (evil inclination), מלכות הרשעה/סטרא אחרא (the evil kingdom), מלך זקן וכסיל (foolish old king as anti-wisdom), מצרים (Egypt/exile as anti-prayer). The הטבע-as-evil-force package is distinct from all of these. It is not the yetzer hara (personal temptation), not the sitra achra (cosmic evil kingdom), not exile (political/spiritual displacement). Rather, it is the philosophical-naturalistic worldview — the claim that the universe is a closed causal system with no room for prayer or miracle. This is a unique conceptual domain: the ENLIGHTENMENT/PHILOSOPHICAL opponent of faith, as opposed to the mystical-evil opponent (sitra achra) or the psychological opponent (yetzer hara). Rebbe Nachman's explicit engagement with 'the philosophers' (הַפִּילוֹסוֹפִים) as a named opposing group is significant — it marks this Torah as addressing a specific intellectual challenge to faith.
nodes: בִּרְכַּת הַמִּינִים (structural counterpart — the blessing that targets this domain)
new_packages.cross_torah_relevance: The הטבע-opposition appears in other Torahs where the Rebbe addresses Enlightenment-era philosophical challenges (naturalism, deism, Epicurean materialism). In Torah #9, for instance, מצרים represents those who 'cover miracles with natural explanations' — a related but distinct domain (Egypt = exile = the state of being unable to pray; הטבע = the philosophical doctrine that prayer is ineffective). A הטבע package type could be valuable as a cross-Torah bridge for all teachings that address the natural-order opposition to faith, complementing the existing מצרים (exile) evil cluster. The מינים/אפיקורסים as the human embodiment of naturalism also has cross-Torah resonance.

observations:
Torah #216 is a 2-sentence Torah. Its contribution to the global package taxonomy is modest but conceptually distinct: it explicitly identifies הַטֶּבַע (Nature/natural determinism) as the opposing force that prayer (specifically the structured 18 blessings) overturns. This is a named, defined opponent — 'what the philosophers call the mother of all living' — which is a philosophical rather than mystical formulation of the evil force.

In the context of the broader Likutay Moharan, this Torah's unique feature is its framing of the adversary as a worldview (naturalism, Epicureanism) rather than a spiritual force (yetzer hara, sitra achra) or historical condition (Egypt, exile). The Birkat HaMinim's structural placement — excluded from the nature-nullifying 18 blessings, yet specifically named as targeting the same human opponents — suggests that the Rebbe saw the philosophical denial of providence as a distinct category requiring its own spiritual counter-measure.

The proposed הטבע package type is a CANDIDATE — not a definitive new taxonomy entry — because Torah #216 provides insufficient bechina-edge data to establish the cluster robustly. If other Torahs in the collection contain similar clusters (הטבע/כפירה/פילוסופים), the case for establishing this as a global package type would be strengthened. The most comparable existing package type is the מצרים-exile cluster (Torah #9, Package 2), which represents the condition of nature being 'closed' to prayer, but even that is phenomenologically different from the explicit philosophical claim that 'nature is the mother of all living.'

Conclusion: The teaching's two-package structure (prayer-transcends vs. nature-constrains) is clean and internally consistent. Package 2 (הטבע וכפירה) represents a potentially novel evil mirror type — the philosophical/rationalist opponent of prayer — that is worth flagging for cross-Torah analysis.
